extracted.intended_audience: U.S. patent examiners and patent owners/agents involved in ex parte reexamination proceedings
extracted.subtask_description: Procedural and substantive rules in the MPEP for conducting, responding to, and appealing ex parte reexamination proceedings, including panel review, final actions, amendment practice after final, and appeal/answer/hearing procedures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of form paragraphs 22.09 and 22.10 for final reexamination actions
rubrics_metrics.description: The final rejection letter should conclude with one of form paragraphs 22.09 or 22.10.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: ¶ 22.09: 'THIS ACTION IS MADE FINAL.' Set a shortened statutory period for response [normally TWO (2) MONTHS], note that extensions under 37 CFR 1.136(a) do not apply in reexamination, explain extensions under 37 CFR 1.550(c) with petition fee under 37 CFR 1.17(g), and state that a timely first response will be construed as a request to extend for one month but response period cannot exceed SIX MONTHS from mailing date. Examiner Note: insert appropriate period in brackets; use one (1) month in court-stayed situations. ¶ 22.10: Use when owner’s amendment necessitated new grounds; similar shortened period and same extension rules; in bracket 1 insert filing date of amendment, bracket 2 insert response period. Final Office action must be signed by a primary examiner.

rubrics_metrics.name: Treatment of art cited by patent owner during prosecution
rubrics_metrics.description: If art is submitted under 37 CFR 1.501 and/or 1.555 and not accompanied by a 37 CFR 1.97(e)-style statement, the examiner may use the art and make the next Office action final provided no other new ground of rejection is introduced based on art not cited in the prior art citation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This only applies where the submission is construed as a prior art citation (an IDS in reexamination). See MPEP § 706.07(a) for further guidance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Signatory authority for final Office actions in reexamination
rubrics_metrics.description: Final Office actions on the merits in a reexamination proceeding must be signed by a primary examiner.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explicit requirement repeated throughout the chapter (e.g., form paragraph 22.10 note).

rubrics_metrics.name: Panel review requirement and scope
rubrics_metrics.description: A panel review will be conducted at each stage of the examiner’s examination in an ex parte reexamination proceeding, other than for notices of informality or incomplete response.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Panel reviews the examiner’s preliminary decision to reject and/or allow the claims prior to issuance of each Office action. Matters outside examiner jurisdiction (petitions, extensions of time, CRU support staff notices) are not reviewed by the panel.

rubrics_metrics.name: Make-up of the panel
rubrics_metrics.description: The panel will consist of three members, one of whom will be a manager, the second member the examiner in charge, and a third member selected by the manager; conferees should be primary examiners or examiners knowledgeable in the technology and/or experienced in reexamination practice.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Majority of those present should be examiners not involved in prior examination/issuance of the patent. An 'original' examiner should be conferee only if most knowledgeable or specific justifiable reason exists.

rubrics_metrics.name: Panel process for issuing Office actions
rubrics_metrics.description: Examiner informs manager of intent to issue an Office action; manager convenes panel to confer and review patentability; if panel confirms preliminary decision, Office action is issued and signed by examiner with two conferees initialing; if not confirmed, examiner reevaluates and issues appropriate action.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Both conferees initial even if one dissents. If examiner in charge disagrees with conference decision, manager will generally assign proceeding to another examiner.

rubrics_metrics.name: Purpose and expected outcomes of the conference
rubrics_metrics.description: Each conference provides a forum to consider all issues of patentability and procedural issues affecting patentability; review by multiple primary examiners aims to reduce perception of undue influence and ensure comprehensive issue resolution.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Conference should detect what the examiner in charge might have missed and provide comprehensive discussion and finding for each issue.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consequences and challenge window for failure to hold panel conference
rubrics_metrics.description: If an Office action is issued without panel review, the patent owner or third party requester must promptly file a paper alerting the Office; any challenge must be made within two weeks of receipt of the Office action or it will not be considered.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Failure to provide panel review, by itself, is not grounds for vacating Office decisions or restarting the reexamination proceeding.

rubrics_metrics.name: After-final practice limits in reexamination
rubrics_metrics.description: Once a proper final rejection is entered in reexamination, the patent owner no longer has a right to unrestricted further prosecution; amendments after final are governed by 37 CFR 1.116 (and after appeal by 37 CFR 41.33).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Patent owner cannot as a matter of right amend finally rejected claims, add new claims, or reinstate canceled claims. An amendment submitted after final but prior to appeal brief requires a showing under 37 CFR 1.116(b) except for amendments that merely cancel claims, adopt examiner’s suggestions, remove issues for appeal, or require cursory review. The first proposed amendment after final will be given sufficient consideration to determine whether it places claims in patentable condition; if not entered in entirety, examiner will briefly explain reasons. Second or subsequent amendments after final considered only to the extent they remove issues for appeal or put a claim in obvious patentable condition.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consideration of evidence and development of issues prior to final
rubrics_metrics.description: Both examiner and patent owner should identify and develop all issues prior to the final Office action, including presentation of evidence under 37 CFR 1.131 and 1.132.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Because reexamined patents cannot become abandoned or be refiled and canceled claims are final in a certificate, thorough development before final is emphasized.

rubrics_metrics.name: Advisory actions and informal/defective response practice after final
rubrics_metrics.description: The practice of giving time to supply omissions or notifying defects via PTOL-475 does not apply after a final Office action; instead, an advisory Office action (form PTOL-467) should be issued explaining omissions or defects in bona fide or informal responses filed after final but before expiration of the response period.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examiner should not issue a PTOL-475 after final; use PTOL-467 with explanation of omission or informality. The practice set forth in MPEP §§ 2266.01 and 2266.02 does not apply after final.

rubrics_metrics.name: Statutory period for response to final rejection and automatic extension rule
rubrics_metrics.description: Statutory period for response to a final rejection in reexamination will normally be two (2) months. The filing of any timely first response to a final rejection is construed as including a request to extend the shortened statutory period for an additional month, automatically, provided total response period does not exceed six months from the date of the final rejection.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Advisory Office actions (PTOL-467) that follow a response after final should inform patent owner of the automatic 1-month extension. Examiner should appropriately extend the period for response in the advisory action so patent owner has sufficient time to consider examiner’s ruling; however, the period may not be extended past six months.

rubrics_metrics.name: Petition under 37 CFR 1.181 after final rejection
rubrics_metrics.description: If patent owner believes a final rejection is improper or an amendment after final complies with 37 CFR 1.116 but was improperly refused entry, patent owner may file a petition under 37 CFR 1.181 requesting withdrawal of the final rejection and reopening of prosecution or requesting entry of the amendment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The petition must be filed within the time period for filing a notice of appeal. Filing a petition under 37 CFR 1.181 does not toll the time period for filing a notice of appeal.

rubrics_metrics.name: Appeal rights and limitations for patent owner and third parties
rubrics_metrics.description: Patent owner involved in reexamination may appeal under section 134 and seek court review under sections 141–145 with respect to adverse decisions to patentability; a third party requester may not appeal or participate in the patent owner’s appeal.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For reexaminations filed before Nov 29, 1999, patent owner may appeal after second rejection; for those filed on/after Nov 29, 1999, patent owner may appeal only after final rejection. Third party requester cannot appeal; the reexamination statute does not provide for review of decisions favoring patentee.

rubrics_metrics.name: Notice of appeal content, timing, and fee requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Notice of appeal need not be signed by patent owner or attorney/agent but must be accompanied by the fee required by 37 CFR 41.20(b)(1). The period for filing the notice of appeal is the period set for response in the last Office action (normally 2 months).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Timely filing of a first response to a final rejection that has a shortened statutory period is construed as requesting an additional month extension (subject to six-month cap). Examiner should not advise patent owner to seek extension under 37 CFR 1.136(a) because that provision does not apply in reexamination.

rubrics_metrics.name: Appeal brief requirements and formatting for reexamination
rubrics_metrics.description: The appeal brief must set forth the authorities and arguments relied on, include a summary of claimed subject matter referring to specification pages/lines and drawings by reference characters, and include a copy of the claims involved. The copy of claims on appeal must include all underlining and bracketing as required by 37 CFR 1.530(f); new claims should be completely underlined.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A fee per 37 CFR 41.20(b)(2) is required when filing the brief for the first time in a particular reexamination proceeding. Only one copy of the appeal brief is required; where third party requester exists, serve a copy on them. In merged proceedings, provide one original copy per reexamination proceeding/reissue application and serve third party requesters. Claims copy should be double spaced and start on a new page. Briefs must be responsive to every ground of rejection and should fully state appellant's position so no search of the record is required.

rubrics_metrics.name: Time for filing appeal brief and extensions
rubrics_metrics.description: Time for filing the appeal brief is two months from the date of the appeal. Petitions for extension (with fee) to the CRU or Technology Center Director may be filed for additional time (usually 1 month) with reasons; the Director may grant up to 1 month for sufficient cause.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Requests for more than one month will be decided by the CRU or TC Director but will not be granted unless extraordinary circumstances (e.g., death, incapacitation). Time extended is added to the last calendar day of the original period (not shifted when last day falls on weekend/holiday).

rubrics_metrics.name: Handling defective appeal briefs
rubrics_metrics.description: Where an appeal brief is defective, the examiner will notify the patent owner using PTOL-462R and provide a one-month period to cure defects; if defects are not included in form items 1-9, box 10 is checked and an attachment explains the defect(s).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If examiner fails to identify defects and give one month, the Board may return the file to the examiner for compliance. If record indicates intentional failure to respond to any ground, examiner should inform the Board; Board may summarily sustain the rejection. The mere filing of a paper entitled 'brief' does not ensure compliance with 37 CFR 41.37; lack of any argument as to a ground may be summarily sustained; lack of persuasive argument may be decided on merits but could be affirmance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Defective notice of appeal cure procedure
rubrics_metrics.description: Where a notice of appeal is defective, the patent owner will be notified using form PTOL-475 and given a 1-month or 30-day (whichever is longer) period to cure the defects.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If patent owner does not timely file a notice of appeal and/or appropriate fee, patent owner will be notified that the appeal is dismissed (use PTOL-468) and reexamination prosecution is terminated; a Notice of Intent to Issue Ex Parte Reexamination Certificate (NIRC) will be issued indicating claims' status at time of final rejection (or after second rejection where appeal was taken earlier).

rubrics_metrics.name: Examiner’s answer and procedures when new ground of rejection is asserted
rubrics_metrics.description: Primary examiner may furnish a written answer to the appeal brief. If the examiner’s answer contains a rejection designated as a new ground of rejection, appellant must within two months either (1) request reopening of prosecution by filing a reply under § 1.111 with or without amendment or submission of affidavits/evidence relevant to the new ground, or (2) maintain the appeal by filing a reply brief under § 41.41 addressing each new ground as required by § 41.37(c)(1)(vii).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A request to reopen prosecution will be treated as a request to withdraw the appeal. A reply brief may not be accompanied by amendments/affidavits/evidence; if it is, it shall be treated as a request to reopen prosecution. Extensions under § 1.136(a) for patent applications are not applicable to these time periods; see § 1.550(c) for reexamination extensions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Supplemental examiner’s answer and replies to reply briefs
rubrics_metrics.description: Where appellant files a timely reply brief or supplemental examiner’s answer, the examiner may (A) acknowledge receipt and entry of the reply brief, (B) reopen prosecution to respond to the reply brief, or (C) furnish a supplemental examiner’s answer responding to any new issue raised in the reply brief.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A supplemental examiner’s answer responding to a reply brief may not include a new ground of rejection (see 37 CFR 41.43(a)(2)). A supplemental examiner’s answer, other than to respond to new issues in a reply brief, is not permitted unless the proceeding has been remanded by the Board.

rubrics_metrics.name: Oral hearing request and public access rules
rubrics_metrics.description: If appellant desires an oral hearing, a written request with fee (37 CFR 41.20(b)(3)) must be filed within 2 months after the examiner’s answer or supplemental examiner’s answer; the time for requesting an oral hearing may not be extended.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: No appellant may participate in an oral hearing unless request and fee are timely filed. For reexamination appeals, oral hearings are open to the public as observers unless appellant petitions under 37 CFR 41.3 that the hearing not be open, presents sufficient reasons, pays petition fee per 37 CFR 41.20(a), and petition is granted. See MPEP § 1209 for more.

rubrics_metrics.name: Board decisions and post-decision procedures; appeal to courts
rubrics_metrics.description: MPEP §§ 1213–1214 and related sections govern Board decisions and procedures after Board conclusion for both applications and ex parte reexamination proceedings. A patent owner not satisfied with the Board may seek judicial review, with differing options depending on whether reexamination was filed before or on/after Nov 29, 1999.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For reexams filed before Nov 29, 1999, appeal to either the Federal Circuit (35 U.S.C. 141) or the D.D.C. (35 U.S.C. 145) was available; for those filed on/after Nov 29, 1999, appeal is to the Federal Circuit only. A third party requester may not seek judicial review, though courts have permitted intervention in some cases; intervenors have no standing to appeal the court’s decision. See MPEP §§ 1213–1216 for details.
